content:
The Global Korea Scholarship (GKS-G) is the Korean government's flagship fully funded award for international students: full tuition, a monthly allowance of KRW 900,000 for graduate students, return airfare and a compulsory one-year Korean language course, all managed by NIIED under the Ministry of Education. For the 2027 intake, the embassy-track window falls in February–March 2027 — applications through Korean embassies close in mid-February, with the university track following.

What GKS-G covers

ComponentValue (standard GKS-G guidelines)
TuitionFull, up to the programme cap + KRW 5,000,000/year overflow support if needed
Monthly allowanceKRW 900,000 (graduate degree students)
Korean language training1 year, funded, before the degree begins
AirfareEconomy round trip, once in and once out
Settlement/arrival supportOne-off allowances under the standard guidelines
InsuranceNational Health Insurance covered during the scholarship
Research supportSemester-linked professor research support for degree research
Degree levelsMaster's and PhD (GKS-U covers bachelor's separately)

The scholarship runs for the standard programme length plus the Korean language year — plan for a 2-year master's to mean 3 years in Korea. Scholars who reach TOPIK level 3+ before arrival can sometimes skip part of the language year and receive an exemption allowance instead.

[[chart:gks-compare]]

Embassy track vs university track

Embassy trackUniversity track
Where you applyKorean embassy in your countryDirectly to the Korean university
WindowFebruary–March 2027 (listing: closes ~15 Feb)Typically March–April 2027 (varies by university)
CompetitionCountry quota (a few seats per country)University quota (Korean + international students compete)
Best forMost applicants; no university choice needed upfrontApplicants with a specific university or supervisor in mind
DocumentsOne embassy submission, 3 university choicesPer-university application

You may apply through only one track — applying to both disqualifies you.

Who is eligible

  • Age under 40, and for the graduate track a bachelor's degree (for master's) or master's (for PhD) — see our guide if you are weighing PhD study without a master's.
  • GPAA above 80% on the GKS grade scale — the embassies convert your transcript; our grade conversion guide helps you estimate where you stand.
  • Applicant and parents not Korean citizens (with narrow exceptions for overseas Koreans).
  • English evidence depends on the track and university — many accept prior English-taught degrees; some ask for IELTS/TOEFL. Our IELTS alternatives guide covers the common substitutes.

How the selection works

  1. Embassy shortlist (round 1): document screening — the personal statement and study plan decide most of it.
  2. NIIED screening (round 2): quota allocation across countries.
  3. University placement (round 3): your three choices are matched with available slots; strong applicants usually get their first or second choice.

The personal statement should explain why Korea, why this field and what you will do with it at home — GKS is a soft-power programme and returns to your country are part of the deal. Structure it like our personal statement examples, but with Korea-specific specificity.

GKS monthly allowance in context

KRW 900,000 is roughly €590–620/month depending on the exchange rate — modest, but Korean universities provide subsidized dormitories (often KRW 300,000–600,000/semester) and campus meals are cheap. GKS scholars in regional cities report comfortable living; Seoul is tighter. Compare with other government scholarships:

ScholarshipMonthly allowance (approx.)Extras
GKS (Korea)KRW 900,000 (≈€600)Tuition + airfare + language year
MEXT (Japan)¥143,000–145,000 (≈€850–880)Tuition + airfare
Türkiye BurslarıTL 9,500–13,000 by levelTuition + accommodation + flights
Stipendium Hungaricum (Hungary)HUF ~43,700 (BA/MA) stipend + housingTuition covered
Chevening (UK)Living allowance set by London/national rateTuition cap + flights

Questions applicants often ask

Can I choose my university? Embassy track: three ranked choices from the designated list; placement is confirmed after selection.

Do I need TOPIK (Korean)? No for admission — that is what the language year is for — but TOPIK 3+ before arrival unlocks benefits.

What about a PhD under GKS? Fully covered like the master's; pair it with our supervisor-contact guide if your department expects a supervisor match.

Documents checklist (embassy track)

DocumentNotes
Application formNIIED's official form — latest version only
Personal statementThe centrepiece: why Korea, why this field, what after
Study plan / research proposalConcrete semester-by-semester plan beats ambition statements
Two recommendation lettersAcademic; sealed or verified per embassy rules
Bachelor's/master's transcripts + diplomasApostilled; with English translations
Proof of citizenship (applicant + parents)Passports or national ID copies — commonly overlooked
Proof of Korean proficiency (optional)TOPIK certificate if you have one — boosts placement
Health certificateOnly after passing round 1, in the embassy's format

Embassies differ on whether they want originals, copies or scans in round 1 — read your embassy's notice. One mismatched checklist item is the most common reason files are returned unreviewed.

Five mistakes that sink GKS applications

  1. Generic statements — "Korea has advanced technology" appears in half of all applications; naming your target department's specific professors and labs signals seriousness.
  2. Applying through both tracks — automatic disqualification.
  3. Missing parents' citizenship proof — required even when it feels irrelevant.
  4. Choosing only Seoul universities — competition concentrates there; regional universities admit far more scholars per applicant.
  5. Transcript conversions without scale — include your university's grading scale so the 80% threshold can be verified; see our grade conversion guide.

For the writing itself, our personal statement structure transfers directly — swap UK references for Korean university specifics.
